name: Nifty 50 · EMA 21 / EMA 105 · 15-minute · always in
rule: BUY when a 15-minute candle closes with EMA 21 above EMA 105. The order fills at the next candle's open.
SELL (short) when a 15-minute candle closes with EMA 21 below EMA 105. The position flips straight from BUY to SELL: always in a trade.
No stop and no target: the next crossover is the exit. Positions are held overnight.
0.035% of price on every buy and every sell. Rupees: 1 lot = 65, and 10 lots.
why: Picked from 2,055 EMA rules on Nifty (10-minute, 15-minute, 1-hour, 2-hour and daily candles; BUY+SELL, BUY only, SELL only).
It made money in every year since July 2023, including 2026 when Nifty fell, and did as well after 1 Jan 2025 as before.
The rules next to it (EMA 13, 15, 20, 25 against EMA 100, 105, 144) also made money every year, so 21 / 105 is not a lucky pair.

now.what: Stays BUY until EMA 21 crosses below EMA 105. One single 15-minute close below about 19,026.83 would do it right now; normally it comes after a slide over many candles.

limits: Picked after looking at this same history. The 10-minute EMA 8 / 200 made more in total but fell to +506 points in 2026; this one was steadier.
About 64% of trades lose. The profit comes from a few long trends, and long losing runs are normal.
Positions are held overnight, so an opening gap can move the trade a long way before you can act.
Fills are assumed exactly at each 15-minute open. 10 lots of 65 is about Rs 1.6 crore of Nifty: check margin before trading that size.
TradingView's 15-minute candles can differ by a few points, so a signal there can be one candle apart.
Paper research. Not SEBI-registered advice. No orders are placed by this website.
